Office of Special Relief Commissioner said more than one lakh people, including close to 10,000 pregnant women, have been shifted to safer places. items.title: U.S. Treasury yields: investors weigh the state of the U.S. economy
items.excerpt: Published Thu, Nov 19 2026 4:52 AM EST Sawdah Bhaimiya U.S. Treasury yields crawled higher on Thursday as investors digested minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting released the previous day. The benchmark 10-year Treasury, 30-year Treasury Add To Watchlist, and 2-year Treasury yields were all up 1 basis point, to 5.425%, 5.084% and 4.815%, respectively. One basis point equals 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions. Investors parsed through the Federal Open Market Committee's meeting minutes on Wednesday, which showed that policymakers expressed confidence in hiking interest rates in December, but are holding off as they collect more information. AI dominated the discussions with concern that the technology would be "a material source of inflation risk." Fed Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC in an interview on Wednesday that a half-percentage-point hike is likely necessary at the central bank's meeting on Dec. 8 and 9, adding that the Fed may need to reverse last year's three-quarter-point reduction and do more. "You might need to, like, shock people," Waller told CNBC's Steve Liesman on " Squawk Box." "I'm very, very concerned about inflation. It's kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out," he said. Traders are now pricing in a 95% chance of a quarter-percentage-point rate hike, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool. Investors will now await Thursday's weekly initial jobless claims data and Friday's preliminary Michigan consumer sentiment.

items.title: Waller says on CNBC the Fed needs to get more aggressive in inflation response By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - US Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller said on Wednesday the central bank needs to get more aggressive in its response to inflation that he fears is changing public psychology about prices, and either approve a half-point hike at the December meeting or communicate a faster pace of hikes in 2027. Inflation is "heading in the wrong direction and it is spreading out," Waller said on CNBC, noting that many of the items with faster-rising prices now are in the services sector and largely beyond the influence of high oil costs and other temporary factors. "If you really want to get it down you’ve got to start taking aggressive actions," either through a larger half-point increase at the coming December 8-9 meeting, or using the post-meeting statement or Chairman Kevin Warsh’s press conference to set market expectations for further hikes.

items.title: Core inflation is 0.5 point lower by CPI than by PCE, and Fed minutes call it unusual | FinanceInTime
items.excerpt: ## Total inflation barely differs, core inflation does The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said the consumer price index (CPI) rose 3.7% in the 12 months to September, after 3.4% in the 12 months to August. The Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) said the PCE price index, its measure of prices for personal consumption expenditures, rose 3.6% from a year earlier in September, after 3.4% in August. Excluding food and energy, the picture splits. Core CPI rose 2.6% over the year to September, following 2.4% in August. Core PCE rose 3.1% in September, after 3.0% in August. Subtracting, the core CPI ran 0.5 percentage point below core PCE in September and 0.6 point below in August (computed from the four published rates). Total CPI was 0.1 point above total PCE in September and equal to it in August (computed). The Fed sets its 2% goal in PCE terms: the Committee judges that inflation at 2% "as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures" fits its mandate over the longer run. So the measure with the higher core reading is the one the Committee targets. ... Energy was the main ... The BLS said gasoline rose 9.1% in September and accounted for over half of the monthly increase in the all-items index, and the energy index rose 5.2% on the month and 20.4% over the 12 months to September. Energy carries a different weight in each index, and the releases do not state the weights, so the data here do not show how much of the headline similarity comes from energy. ## October's CPI has no annual rate The October CPI report shows the CPI rose 0.4% on the month after 0.6% in September, with core prices up 0.3% for a third month. The BLS said it did not collect survey data for October 2025 because of a lapse in appropriations, so it cannot publish 12-month changes for October 2026 for indexes where October 2025 data are unavailable. The annual CPI comparison with PCE therefore stops at September until November data arrive; the BEA's October PCE release is due on November 25, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. EST, according to its September release. ## What Fed officials said about the discrepancy The minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting, released on November 18, show the staff estimated PCE inflation of 3.6% in September and core PCE of 3.1%, and attributed higher inflation largely to earlier tariff increases, higher energy prices and upward pressure on goods prices tied to the AI buildout. Some participants raised the gap directly. A few cautioned that market-based inflation expectations, derived from the pricing of securities indexed to the CPI, "might be difficult to interpret" given "an unusual discrepancy between CPI and PCE inflation rates." The minutes do not say what causes the discrepancy. Participants also pointed to elevated inflation in market-based core nonhousing services and to measures of underlying inflation that remained above 2%. Almost all judged that further action to raise the target range would likely be appropriate, and a couple said an increase of more than 25 basis points could warrant consideration at the next meeting if inflation data were unfavorable. That meeting is on December 8-9.

items.excerpt: Amazon's Bezos says he helped pick Pattinson as Bond Amazon founder and chairman Jeff Bezos said he was heavily involved in selecting "Batman" actor Robert Pattinson to take on the iconic film role of James ​Bond. Bezos spoke at Semafor's Silicon Valley & The World conference on Tuesday, a day after the company announced Pattinson as the next 007. He said Amazon narrowed down a ​larger group and screen-tested five actors by having them perform three scenes in full costume on sets. Harry Styles, Billie Eilish and Cher to headline UK's Glastonbury in 2027 Harry Styles, Sam Fender, Billie Eilish and Cher will headline Britain's Glastonbury next year, the organisers said on their website on Wednesday, as the sold-out festival returns after taking a year off in 2026. British singer Harry Styles, who recently completed a 30-show residency at Madison Square Garden in New York, will play the festival for the first time, while Cher will take the legends slot at the age of 81. ... Spain's High Court opens investigation into women's allegations against Julio Iglesias A Spanish High Court judge has opened a criminal investigation into singer Julio Iglesias after a complaint filed by two former employees alleging sexual offences, assault and degrading treatment, court records showed. The complaint was filed by ⁠rights group Women's Link Worldwide on behalf of two women who said they worked in Iglesias' Caribbean residences for 10 months in 2021, following an investigation by US broadcaster Univision and Spanish outlet elDiario.es. The fourth installment in the "Fockers" comedy film franchise comes 26 years after Stiller and Robert De Niro introduced audiences ⁠to ​quarrelling male nurse Greg Focker and retired CIA operative Jack Byrnes in "Meet the Parents".

items.title: Entertainment News Live Updates Today (November 19, 2026): Alia Bhatt On ‘Unequal’ Marriage With Ranbir Kapoor | Mysskin Left Keerthy Suresh Uncomfortable At Sathyavan Savithiri Press Conference | Ramayana Box Office Update - Filmibeat
items.excerpt: ## Saif Ali Khan Receives Death Threat Bollywood actor Saif Ali Khan has reportedly received a death threat from someone claiming to be Zeeshan Akhtar, who is wanted in connection with the 2024 murder of politician Baba Siddique. The police are now trying to establish whether Akhtar was actually involved in sending the threat or if someone else used his name to target celebrities and create trouble for law enforcement agencies. This is not the first such incident reported this month. Actors Tusshar Kapoor and Ayushmann Khurrana had also received similar threats earlier. Police arrested 30-year-old Vaibhav Mishra, an IIT graduate from Bengaluru, in connection with both cases. Investigators found no links between Mishra and any criminal gang. He allegedly used artificial intelligence (AI) to send the threatening messages. ... ## Ramayana Box Office Collection Day 14 Ramayana has surpassed Aditya Dhar's Dhurandhar at the Indian box office within just two weeks of its release. According to Sacnilk, the film earned Rs. 23.20 crore net in India on Day 14, taking its total domestic net collection to Rs. 844.40 crore. Its India gross collection has now reached Rs. 1,009.05 crore. With this, Ramayana has moved ahead of Dhurandhar, which had collected Rs. 840.20 crore net in India after its release in December last year. The achievement comes just 14 days into Ramayana's theatrical run. However, the film's overseas performance appears to be slowing down. It added Rs. 8 crore gross from international markets on Day 14, taking its overseas gross collection to Rs. 510 crore. Meanwhile, its worldwide gross collection has reached Rs. 1,519.05 crore. ... Speaking to TIME magazine as part of its TIME100 Next India feature, Alia Bhatt addressed the online discussions about her marriage to Ranbir Kapoor and the claims that she is in an ‘unequal marriage’. The actress called such assumptions offensive, saying people were reducing her to someone who would silently suffer in an imaginary situation. Alia also suggested that the speculation could stem from the fact that her relationship does not follow conventional ideas of marriage. Explaining what makes her bond with Ranbir special, she said, "The bedrock of any relationship is when you feel seen without putting any effort, and feel heard without saying anything—that’s Ranbir for me, and that’s our reality."

items.title: Chris Pratt to Star in Paramount Pictures' 'The Traveler'
items.excerpt: Chris Pratt is set to headline Paramount Pictures’ adaptation of The Traveler, based on the novel by Joseph Eckert. The project is part of the Guardians of the Galaxy star’s first-look three-year producing deal with the Melrose Ave lot through his Indivisible production banner, with the potential to star in select projects.
